claims.text: As-cast or homogenized thermomechanically processed multi-component concentrated alloys generally have predominantly random solid-solution microstructures.
Processing conditions that do not enhance local chemical order can produce a more randomized chemical configuration for the baseline.
Controlled heat treatment can enhance local chemical order while retaining the alloy's overall composition.
Minor compositional adjustment can be used to enhance local chemical order or its associated fault-energy fluctuations.
Local chemical order is associated with spatial variations in generalized planar or shear-fault energies in concentrated alloys.
Increasing local chemical order produces larger spatial fluctuations in shear-fault energy.
The rugged energy landscape associated with local chemical order raises activation barriers and causes segment-scale dislocation pinning and detrapping.
Higher local chemical order causes more frequent dislocation pinning than a lower-order baseline.
Enhanced local chemical order increases lattice resistance to dislocation motion and thereby raises yield strength.
Local chemical order can alter the selection of dislocation pathways, including slip, faulting, and twinning.
Samples with higher local chemical order will exhibit higher yield strength than composition- and grain-structure-matched samples with lower local chemical order.
Samples with higher local chemical order will exhibit more rugged or segmented dislocation lines and altered slip patterns relative to the lower-order baseline.
Local chemical order and fault-energy fluctuations are a governing cause of strength and deformation behavior in FCC multi-component concentrated alloys.
The proposed mechanism should hold from room temperature to moderately elevated temperatures.
The proposed mechanism should hold from quasi-static to moderately dynamic strain rates.
Lattice distortion may overlap with local chemical order as an alternative contribution to dislocation resistance and strengthening.

contradictions.description: The intervention permits a minor compositional adjustment while simultaneously requiring overall composition to remain constant; a compositional adjustment necessarily changes the nominal composition unless separately defined as a distinct comparison.
